Kevin (Customer): Hey team, we're seeing streaming responses cut off midstream when a device switches networks (WiFi -> cellular). The client shows some partial tokens then stops, no [DONE], no reconnect. Repro is pretty consistent on our QA Android 13 devices by toggling wifi.

Maria (Support): thanks for the report. Can you paste the client logs and the exact request (headers/body)? Which SDK and version?

Kevin (Customer): using mobile-sdk-js v1.4.2 (we rely on EventSource). Request to /v1/streams chat with stream=true. We set a session_id header per-request. Client log snippet:

[2026-02-20T09:12:01Z] EventSource opened
[2026-02-20T09:12:17Z] received data: "data: {\"delta\":"Hel"}"
[2026-02-20T09:12:18Z] network change wlan->cellular
[2026-02-20T09:12:19Z] EventSource error (readyState=2)
[2026-02-20T09:12:19Z] connection reset by peer

Maria (Support): got it. On the server side do you see any 4xx/5xx or connection resets around that time? Any auth failures afterwards?

Kevin (Customer): we don't see auth errors tied to these events. Our server logs show:

[2026-02-20T09:12:18Z] stream_open session_id=xyz789 peer_ip=172.31.16.5
[2026-02-20T09:12:19Z] client_disconnect session_id=xyz789 reason=TCP_RESET
[2026-02-20T09:12:19Z] stream_closed session_id=xyz789 status=499

Dan (Eng): 499 follows nginx semantics (client closed before server sent final). NAT rebinding during WiFi->cell swap will change the TCP 4-tuple and often result in kernel-level RSTs. EventSource in browsers/clients doesn't always auto-reopen after an OS-triggered socket close. Does your app ever explicitly recreate the EventSource on error? Share code.

Kevin (Customer): code is simple, we just new EventSource(url) and log errors. We don't spawn a fresh EventSource because we worry about duplicating partial events. Snippet:

const es = new EventSource(url);
es.onmessage = (e) => handleDelta(JSON.parse(e.data));
es.onerror = (e) => console.warn('es error', e);

Aisha (SRE): mobile NAT rebinding is the likely culprit. Two short-term approaches: 1) client reconnects and supplies a resume cursor/last-event-id so server can emit the remainder or 2) server sends stronger keepalives to keep mobile OS from deeming the socket dead. Do we support resumable SSE today? I thought not.

Dan (Eng): correct, no official resume. session_id is only metadata (billing/annotation), not resume. Implementing true resume is hard (model state, KV cache). Short term we can accept a best-effort resume header X-Redwood-Resume: <cursor> for idempotent clients and do a naive stitch, and the SDK can retry. Also reduce keepalive interval and ensure LB timeouts are tuned.

Maria (Support): customer is using this for a live partial-transcription UI so UX impact is high. We'll mark this urgent.

Kevin (Customer): ideally the SDK would attempt one reconnect automatically and provide a last-event marker so we avoid losing the rest. We can dedupe tokens by event id on the client.

Dan (Eng): agreed. Proposed immediate actions:
- SDK: implement reconnect-on-error policy (1-2 retries) that includes X-Redwood-Resume set to lastEventId (or cursor).
- Server: accept X-Redwood-Resume and attempt best-effort continuation (may cause duplicate final tokens), and lower keepalive comments to 15s.
- Infra: check LB idle timeout and increase for mobile streams if necessary.

deploy-bot: Canary: reduce-keepalive-interval started on staging (run-4612)

Aisha (SRE): checked LB logs for the repro window 7. Idle timeout is 60s. We currently emit SSE comments roughly every 30s; for these repros we saw last comment at 09:11:58 and the client went away ~21s later when it switched networks. Mobile OS often closes sockets on IP change rather than letting TCP teardown gracefully.

Dan (Eng): SDK reconnect sketch for mobile-js (to be PR'd):
function streamWithResume(url) {
  let lastEventId = null;
  function connect() {
    const headers = lastEventId ? { 'X-Redwood-Resume': lastEventId } : {};
    const es = new EventSource(url, { headers });
    es.onmessage = e => { lastEventId = e.lastEventId || lastEventId; handleDelta(JSON.parse(e.data)); }
    es.onerror = e => { es.close(); setTimeout(connect, 1000); }
  }
  connect();
}

Maria (Support): opening ticket SUP-8921 and assigning to Dan + Aisha. Kevin, can you attach a pcap or ngrok capture and the exact device/os build? Also indicate whether the app was backgrounded or in foreground during the repro.

Kevin (Customer): i'll gather ngrok tcpdump and app logs. repro steps: open stream, wait a few tokens, toggle wifi off. i'll attach the capture shortly.
